jobs.title: Hardware Penetration Tester
jobs.excerpt: Packetlabs is a cybersecurity consulting firm specializing in advanced Penetration Testing.
jobs.description:
Packetlabs is a cybersecurity consulting firm specializing in advanced Penetration Testing. We exist to eliminate the false sense of security that comes from shallow testing and checkbox-driven assessments. Our slogan, "Ready for more than a VA scan?", reflects a simple standard: real security work should be rigorous, manual, and built to uncover what automated approaches miss. Our clients span government, technology, law enforcement, retail, healthcare, and financial services, and they rely on us because credibility matters when the stakes are high.

Packetlabs is looking for an Penetration Tester - Hardware to lead security assessments of embedded and IoT devices, the physical products where a vulnerability lives in silicon, firmware, and board layout, rather than in a web request. The Ethical Hacker - Hardware is a specialized technical role focused on assessing embedded systems across all industries, from consumer IoT to industrial and connected devices. This role involves getting hands-on with a device, opening it up, and proving what an attacker with physical or local access can really do.

This role requires the rare combination of offensive security instinct and genuine hardware fundamentals. You will work directly with clients to understand their devices and deliver findings that improve security posture.

Who we are looking for

  • No egos, ever. Egos don't belong at Packetlabs. The more you learn, the less you know. You stay humble, ask questions, and work to help clients improve their security.
  • Customer-first mentality. You are an excellent communicator with clients, project managers, and teammates. You are responsive, reliable, and professional throughout every engagement.
  • You deliver work that you take pride in. Your work is an autograph of your excellence. You hold yourself to a high standard, and it shows in what you produce.
  • Digs deeper into every finding. You don't stop until impact is proven, while understanding that restraint is the right call in sensitive OT environments where high-risk activity is not appropriate.
  • Comfortable being uncomfortable. You move toward obstacles, not away from them. Consulting is not a typical job and requires adapting to rapidly changing environments.
  • Always learning. Cybersecurity changes every day, and you keep up because you want to. You are deeply aware of your skillset and committed to improving it.
  • Self-motivated and dependable. You take ownership of your work and your outcomes without needing to be managed into them.

What you’ll be doing

  • Hardware Penetration Testing
    • Plan and execute end-to-end hardware penetration tests on embedded and IoT devices, against a defined scope and rules of engagement
    • Identify, access, and exploit on-board debug interfaces: JTAG, SWD, UART, and similar, to gain code execution or memory access
    • Extract firmware via debug ports, in-circuit flash reads (SPI / I2C / NAND), or chip-off when required, and analyze it for vulnerabilities
    • Intercept and analyze data on common embedded buses (SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, USB) using logic analyzers and protocol decoders
    • Where in scope, perform side-channel analysis and fault injection (power analysis, voltage/clock glitching) to bypass secure boot, readout protection, or authentication
  • Firmware Analysis & Reverse Engineering
    • Reverse engineer firmware and embedded binaries (Ghidra, IDA, Binwalk, etc.) to find logic flaws, hardcoded secrets, and exploitable conditions
    • Assess physical attack surface, tamper resistance, and key/secret storage
    • Distinguish between theoretical and operationally relevant risk to keep findings actionable
  • Client Advisory & Remediation
    • Write high-quality technical reports and present findings to client stakeholders, both technical and non-technical
    • Advise on practical, prioritized remediation that clients can act on
    • Build client confidence through credibility, clear communication, and proven impact
  • Methodology, Research & Continuous Improvement
    • Build and maintain lab tooling, test rigs, and internal methodology
    • Contribute to research, responsible disclosure, and internal knowledge-sharing
    • Stay current on hardware attack techniques, embedded architectures, and defensive controls
    • Help raise the standard of hardware security work across the firm

What success looks like

  • Clients gain a clear, accurate understanding of their hardware risk, backed by proven, reproducible impact
  • Findings are credible, actionable, and land for both technical and leadership audiences
  • Engagements are delivered to a consistently high standard with strong client confidence
  • Scope and rules of engagement are managed well as engagements evolve, with risk surfaced early and clearly
  • Packetlabs' hardware testing methodology and lab capability continue to mature through your contribution
  • Clients trust Packetlabs as the partner that can break their hardware before someone else does

Education and Experience

  • A graduate of an Information Security, Computer Science, or Computer/Electrical Engineering degree program (or equivalent hands-on experience)
  • Strong electronics fundamentals. Able to read schematics and datasheets and reason about a board from them
  • Hands-on soldering ability, including surface-mount (SMD) rework and basic chip removal
  • Demonstrated experience accessing debug interfaces (JTAG, SWD, UART) and extracting firmware from real devices
  • Comfort with core bench instruments: logic analyzer, oscilloscope, and multimeter
  • Firmware reverse-engineering skills and scripting proficiency in Python, plus enough C to read embedded code
  • Familiarity with common embedded architectures (ARM/Cortex-M, MIPS, AVR, RISC-V) and RTOS/bare-metal concepts
  • Clear written and verbal communication.
  • Nice to have (one or more would be an asset):
    • Side-channel / fault-injection experience (e.g., ChipWhisperer)
    • RF and wireless work: SDR, BLE, sub-GHz, Wi-Fi
    • Knowledge of secure boot chains, TEEs, secure elements, and HSMs
    • PCB design familiarity (KiCad / Altium) for understanding target boards
    • Published CVEs, conference talks, CTF placements, or open-source tooling
    • Relevant certifications (e.g., OSCP for breadth, or hardware-focused training)

Why us?

  • The opportunity to work on high-stakes hardware engagements where your judgment and bench skills genuinely matter
  • Receive immediate and ongoing offensive security training, mentorship, and professional development to advance your technical capabilities
  • Play a key role in shaping the growth, direction, and methodology of Packetlabs' expanding hardware practice
  • A leadership team that values substance, quality, and disciplined execution
  • Collaboration with a highly skilled team of security professionals who are passionate about technical excellence and raising the bar
  • Competitive compensation and growth opportunity
  • Flexible work environment that empowers employees to do their best work
  • Fully remote within Canada

As a Post Doctoral Scientist at Gilead, you will support the Structural Biology and Chemistry department; working on AI/ML for Small Molecule Drug Discovery. A highly motivated, attentive and self-driven postdoctoral researcher candidate will join the Computational Modeling Group as part of a three-year postdoctoral training program

  • Investigate the feasibility of utilizing machine learning models to predict properties of heterobifunctional degraders (EPSA, permeability, etc.) using either SMILES strings or three-dimensional conformational ensembles as starting points.

Job Title: Master Class - Business Consultant - Life Sciences Commercial (Germany)

Job Location: Berlin, Germany

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full-time

Job Seniority Level:

Veeva Systems is building the industry cloud for Life Sciences to help companies work in a more efficient and connected way. Learn more about our products, vision and values, and status as a public benefit corporation on our website.

Consulting is changing, and we’re not like other firms. Veeva Business Consulting was launched in 2019 and has grown quickly and organically to a global organization of over 400 people. Our team is focused on making the Life Sciences industry more efficient and effective through software, data, and consulting working together.

We expect significant growth in Business Consulting as we look towards 2030, and are looking for great people to make it happen.

The Role

We are hiring high potential people who are early in their careers and want to pivot into Life Sciences Consulting through our Master Class Program.

Breaking into business consulting after starting your career down a different path can be hard. As an alternative to an MBA, this program is intentionally designed as the entry path to shape experienced professionals as Business Consultants capable of making an impact for the Life Sciences industry.

Early in the program, you will own key workstreams on customer-facing engagements to create high-impact business solutions while collaborating with team members at all levels of Veeva. You will be given the tools and resources to accelerate your consulting skills development.

Our Business Consulting team builds effective business and operational improvement strategies powered by Veeva’s unique industry insights, and market-leading technology. Our offerings are focused on speeding drug development, launching treatments more effectively, and shaping the best engagement for our customers.

If you’re graduating with an advanced degree or have 3-5 years of industry experience and are excited to pivot your career into consulting for a critical industry, Master Class is for you.

The anticipated start date is April 2027.

What You'll Do

    • Support and deliver all components of customer engagements (e.g., customer communications, workshops, stakeholder interviews, process and data analysis, managing timelines)
    • Collaborate with Business Consultants to create deliverables that optimize customer operating and engagement models, processes, and business performance
    • Leverage Veeva’s software and data to pull through tangible business and operational solutions
REQUIREMENTS | We are looking for people who meet the following requirements:
    • 3-5 years of experience from one of the following paths: Life Sciences Industry experience; Advanced Degree (PhD, PharmD, MD); or Other non-Consulting work experience
    • Desire to work within an intense, challenging program and environment
    • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
    • A problem-solving mindset: anticipating issues early, analyzing, and proactively finding solutions
    • A process-driven person who loves digging into operations, numbers, and other data to find opportunities for improvement
    • High work ethic. Veeva is a hard-working company
    • High integrity and honesty. Veeva is a PBC and a “do the right thing” company, and we expect that from all employees
    • Willingness to travel up to 20% of your time per year. Travel varies per customer engagement, coworking, internal meetings, and events with your team
THE PROCESS | Our process is different than most. It is designed to be fast, efficient and respectful. Here are the steps:
    • You submit your resume, short cover letter of questions, and take a personality test
    • Within one week we will notify you via email if we would like to go to the next step or not
    • The next step is a 45-minute interview with the Executive Leader of the practice, followed by a case exercise. You will have one week to prepare for the case exercise
    • Within one week after this step, we will give you an offer, or let you know that we do not wish to move forward
    • You will have two weeks to accept our offer or not. If you accept, we will hold a spot for you and expect you to show up on your start date. Accepting an offer and continuing to interview would be an ethical violation in our view

Compensation

    • Starting Salary: 70,000 EUR
    • After one year, if you perform well, you will receive a significant salary increase and be granted equity

Work Authorization: Qualified candidates should be legally authorized to be employed in the EU.

Work Environment: Veeva is a Work Anywhere company. You can choose to work in an office or remotely from home on any given day of the week. There is no requirement to live near a Veeva office if a candidate is in proximity to an airport and able to meet travel requirements.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

You will utilize your skills, knowledge, and clinical judgement to provide a high standard of care for participants in clinical trials and respond to emergency situations based upon clinical research standards.

Responsibilities:

  • Responsible for all aspects of study site monitoring including routine monitoring and close-out of clinical sites, maintenance of study files, conduct of pre-study and initiation visits; liaise with vendors; and other duties, as assigned -

  • Responsible for all aspects of site management as prescribed in the project plans

  • Ensure the study staff who will conduct the protocol have received the proper materials and instructions to safely enter patients into the study

  • Ensure the protection of study patients by verifying that informed consent procedures and protocol requirements are adhered to according to the applicable regulatory requirements

  • Ensure the integrity of the data submitted on Case Report Forms (CRFs) or other data collection tools by careful source document Monitor data for missing or implausible data

jobs.excerpt: About MoneyHashMoneyHash is building the future of API-based payment infrastructure.
jobs.description:
About MoneyHash

MoneyHash is building the future of API-based payment infrastructure. Our easy-install APIs consolidate the revenue cycle across geographies, functions, and use cases. We're saving our clients time and money, boosting product performance, unlocking new business opportunities, and reducing tech debt.

We're one of the fastest-growing payment infrastructure companies in emerging markets, and we know that building the right team is crucial to realizing our potential. At MoneyHash, we champion human empathy as well as work excellence. Join us and let's explore this journey together!

Your Team

Integrations is where MoneyHash's core promise actually gets built. Every merchant who connects once and reaches dozens of providers is standing on a connection that somebody scoped, briefed, tested and shipped. We add providers and payment methods continuously across MENA and beyond (cards, KNET, Mada, STC Pay, Fawry, wallets, BNPL), and each one is its own small project with its own documentation, quirks, sandbox and failure modes.

You'll own that pipeline. Requests arrive from sales, customer success and merchants: a new provider, a new payment method on a provider we already support, or a new capability on a method that's already live. You work out what each one actually involves, write it down precisely enough that other people can build it, and carry it through to go-live.

You will not write code. You will read a great deal of API documentation.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Own the intake. Every connection request lands with you. Work out whether it's a new provider, a new method, or a capability extension, and check what we've already built before anything starts.
  • Scope at the method level. A provider doesn't "support KWD". It supports KWD on KNET via redirection, with a specific set of operations and no tokenization. Read the provider's documentation and produce that matrix: integration types, currencies, schemes, operations, tokenization, 3DS, webhooks. Mark clearly what the docs don't answer.
  • Find what's missing before engineering does. Which merchant requirements the provider genuinely cannot meet, which features the provider has to switch on for our account, what the sandbox won't let us test.
  • Write the tickets. A self-contained build brief for the external developer, an engineering story with a QA checklist as its acceptance criteria, an error-code mapping table. Short, specific and correct. Our engineers have built dozens of connections and don't need the basics explained back to them.
  • Manage the external developers. Brief them, keep them unblocked, review what comes back, and say no when it isn't right.
  • Run the integrations backlog for a dedicated squad. Sequence the work, keep the pipeline moving, and tell the people waiting where their connection stands.
  • Get it live. Credentials, testing data, QA, launch.

You’ll Be Great for This Role If You

  • Have hands-on experience scoping or delivering payment provider integrations. You've worked through a PSP's API documentation and turned it into something a team could build. This one isn't negotiable.
  • Can read API documentation, JSON payloads and webhook specifications and state precisely what a provider does and does not support (you won't write code)
  • Write short. Much of this job is compressing a 200-page provider doc into a one-page brief somebody can build from without asking you five follow-up questions.
  • Know the difference between authorize, capture, purchase, void and refund, what a webhook can and cannot be trusted for, and why tokenization and recurring are not the same thing
  • Are organized under load, with several connections in flight at once, each waiting on a different person
  • Have worked with external contractors or vendors and can hold them to a specification
Bonus points:
  • MENA/GCC payment methods and local acquiringn
  • Payment orchestration, routing, or failover
  • Error-code mapping, reconciliation, or QA of payment flows
  • Linear, Notion, and writing for engineering audiences

Your First 90 Days

Onboarding here is a designed program, not a stack of documents: structured sessions on how our platform and payments actually work, hands-on sandbox access from day one, and real connections to scope in your first weeks. By the end of it you'll be running the integration pipeline for real.

How We Work at MoneyHash

Beyond your functional responsibilities, everyone at MoneyHash plays a part in shaping our culture and values:

  • Respect. We’re a global team and value diversity, empathy, and honest dialogue.
  • Humility. We give and receive feedback with openness, leaving egos at the door.
  • Flexibility. We adapt quickly, learn constantly, and step up where needed.
  • Willingness to Learn. We embrace growth, celebrate iteration, and treat every mistake as a step forward.

Where we work: Remote-first across EMEA time zones, with an annual in-person retreat to bring the team together.

Compensation Package

Competitive salary - stock options - health insurance - professional development stipend - wellness stipend - tech allowance - equipment financing program - annual in-person retreat - team engagement initiatives

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

The United States Based Salary range for this role is: 140,000-200,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

jobs.title: Strategic Finance Analyst
jobs.excerpt: Actionstep is a pioneer in the development and sale of software-as-a-service (SaaS) products, specializing in the delivery of Legal Practice Management and Legal Accounting software.
jobs.description:
Actionstep is a pioneer in the development and sale of software-as-a-service (SaaS) products, specializing in the delivery of Legal Practice Management and Legal Accounting software. We are a fast-growing, dynamic business with a global customer base of more than 50,000 and a team of over 250 across the USA, Australia, UK, Canada, and New Zealand.

Actionstep is expanding its product portfolio and adding richer AI functionality across the platform to deepen customer value, accelerate cross-sell revenue, and introduce new add-on modules that increase competitive differentiation.

THE PURPOSE OF YOUR ROLE

The Strategic Finance Analyst is a core contributor to Actionstep’s Finance team. The role’s initial focus areas are core FP&A work, including forecasting and profitability analysis; gross margin and pricing analysis; and commission calculations across Sales, Partner, and Operations teams. You will report to the VP of Finance and work closely with the broader Finance and RevOps teams. As Actionstep’s needs evolve, the specific mix of responsibilities may shift, and you may take on additional or different analytical work over time.

ABOUT YOU

You are a strong finance analyst who thinks in numbers first, and you’re just as comfortable in the data and systems behind those numbers as you are in a spreadsheet. You build clean, reliable models and analysis, and you understand that the work behind a recurring deliverable has to be right every time, not most of the time.

You bring real curiosity to the business behind the numbers. You do not just produce an analysis, you ask what it means and whether it should change how the business plans or decides.

You move comfortably between recurring, deadline-driven deliverables and more open-ended strategic analysis, and you know how to prioritize when both compete for your time.

You build trust across Finance and other teams by being accurate, responsive, and clear about what your analysis does and does not say. You take feedback well and ask questions up front rather than guessing.

WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING

The focus areas below reflect the business’s current priorities. As with most roles on a growing team, they may change as those priorities evolve, and may also include support for strategic initiatives such as partnerships or M&A as they arise.

FP&A: Forecasting & Profitability

  • Support the development and maintenance of annual budgets and rolling forecasts.
  • Conduct budget-to-actual variance analysis and support profitability analysis across the business.
  • Build and maintain financial models to support business decisions, including scenario and sensitivity analysis, particularly through the use of AI tools.
  • Contribute datasets and analysis to board and executive reporting materials. Work closely with other members of the Finance team, including the Senior Financial & Systems Analyst, on shared data and reporting priorities.

Pricing & Gross Margin Analysis

  • Conduct gross margin analysis by product, segment, and customer cohort, and identify trends and margin improvement opportunities.
  • Support pricing strategy and annual price increase analysis, including modeling impact across customer segments, for new and existing product lines.
  • Partner with Billing and RevOps to validate pricing and margin data before it reaches leadership.

Commission Calculations

  • Support monthly/quarterly commission calculations for Sales, Partner, and Operations teams, including quality control checks prior to distribution.
  • Partner with Sales, RevOps, and Partner teams to ensure the data behind commission calculations, such as bookings, quotas, and contract terms, is accurate.
  • Investigate and resolve commission discrepancies as they arise.

Data & Systems

  • Partner with the Senior Financial & Systems Analyst on the data and systems behind the company’s business intelligence, recurring reporting, and general analysis efforts.
  • Automate recurring deliverables, such as commission calculations, to reduce manual, spreadsheet-based work over time.
  • Contribute to the infrastructure work, the “plumbing,” that keeps Finance’s data and systems running reliably via a company-wide data warehouse.
  • Help document the business logic behind recurring Finance calculations so it’s repeatable and scalable.
  • Build or maintain dashboards and reporting views that support recurring Finance deliverables.

Flag data quality issues upstream and work with the relevant team to fix them at the source.

Requirements

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field.
  • 1–3 years of proven work experience as a Financial Analyst, or in a similar FP&A, accounting, or business analysis role.
  • Strong Excel skills, including advanced formulas and financial modeling.
  • Working knowledge of SQL and curiosity to learn more.
  • Excellent analytical skills and comfort working with large, sometimes imperfect datasets.
  • Ability to present financial data clearly through reports, charts, and summaries for both financial and non-financial audiences.
  • Hands-on experience with financial or ERP systems.
  • Strong personal accountability for accuracy, particularly on recurring deliverables that affect employee pay.

Preferred

  • Experience in a SaaS or subscription-based business.
  • Experience with NetSuite or a similar ERP platform.
  • Experience with a cloud data warehouse platform (e.g., Snowflake) or BI/reporting tools (e.g., Power BI).
  • Prior experience with sales commission calculations, gross margin analysis, or pricing analysis.

THIS ROLE REPORTS TO

VP of Finance (Christian Ebersol).

METRICS OF SUCCESS

  • Accuracy & reliability: recurring deliverables are accurate and delivered on time, with minimal rework.
  • Analytical value: your analysis is trusted and used by Finance leadership and cross-functional partners in decision-making.
  • Cross-functional trust: partner teams across the business view Finance as a reliable, responsive partner.
  • Growth in scope: demonstrates readiness to take on broader financial planning and strategic analysis responsibilities within 12 to 18 months.

Benefits

  • Medical, dental, vision offerings
  • RRSB with company match
  • Flexible working and PTO
  • Take your birthday off
  • Frequent team-building events
  • Fantastic training and development opportunities

Veeam is the Data and AI Trust Company, specializing in helping organizations ensure their data and AI are fully understood, secured, and resilient to enable the acceleration of safe AI at scale. As the market leader in both data resilience and data security posture management, Veeam is built for the convergence of identity, data, security, and AI risk. About the Role

The Senior Customer Success Specialist (CSS) serves as the customer's trusted technical advisor and primary technical owner, guiding customers through activation, adoption, optimization, expansion, and renewal. In this role, you will develop and execute tailored Customer Success Plans that align technical adoption with business objectives, strengthen resilience posture, and drive measurable outcomes. Leveraging deep expertise across the Veeam portfolio, you will help customers maximize value, improve recovery readiness, advance data resilience maturity, and achieve their desired business goals while partnering closely with Sales, Customer Success leadership, and other Veeam teams.

What You’ll Do

  • Own the technical customer relationship for a portfolio of strategic Enterprise and Commercial Named accounts, serving as a trusted advisor throughout the customer lifecycle.
  • Build, maintain, and advance tailored Customer Success Plans aligned to each customer's business objectives, technical priorities, desired outcomes, and success criteria.
  • Guide customer activation, drive adoption and optimization, and help customers realize measurable value from their investment across the Veeam portfolio.

Bonus Skills

jobs.excerpt: Role SummaryThe Vice President, Payer Account Management is the senior leader accountable for Pfizer's strategic engagement and account management with U.
jobs.description:
Role Summary

The Vice President, Payer Account Management is the senior leader accountable for Pfizer's strategic engagement and account management with U.S. payer customers. Reporting to the Vice President, Strategic Account Management, this role leads the Payer Account Management organization and is responsible for translating Pfizer's portfolio and brand access strategies into coordinated customer strategies, negotiations, and account-level execution that deliver sustainable patient access and strong business outcomes.

The Vice President establishes the strategic direction for Pfizer's payer relationships across national, regional, and government payer segments and ensures a consistent, enterprise approach to customer engagement across the portfolio. The role develops and maintains senior relationships with key payer decision-makers, leads complex negotiations within established governance and decision authorities, and ensures that account strategies balance patient access, portfolio priorities, customer needs, and responsible gross-to-net investment.

The role serves as an important voice of the payer within Pfizer, bringing customer, competitive, reimbursement, policy, and formulary insights back into the organization to inform access strategy, contracting choices, launch preparation, forecasting, and portfolio decisions. This is increasingly important as payer consolidation, benefit design, policy changes, and utilization management continue to influence access decisions.

The Vice President works closely with US Market Access BU leaders, Access Enablement, Market Access Operations, Patient Services, Commercial business leaders, Finance, Medical, Policy, Legal and other enterprise partners to connect strategy through execution and ensure account teams are equipped with the strategies, insights, value propositions, analytics and contracting parameters needed to deliver differentiated access outcomes.

Role Responsibilities


1. Payer Account Strategy & Leadership

  • Set the strategic direction for Pfizer's payer account management organization, ensuring customer engagement is aligned to portfolio priorities, brand access objectives and broader U.S. business goals.
  • Lead development and execution of integrated payer account strategies across national, regional and government payer customers.
  • Translate enterprise and BU access priorities into clear, actionable account plans with defined objectives, customer strategies, negotiation priorities and measures of success.
  • Ensure account plans take a portfolio-level view of Pfizer's relationship with each customer, balancing individual brand objectives with broader enterprise considerations.
  • Establish clear priorities and expectations for payer account teams and ensure disciplined execution against the most important access opportunities and risks.
  • Identify opportunities to strengthen Pfizer's strategic position with payer customers through more integrated, forward-looking and differentiated engagement.

2. Senior Payer Customer Leadership

  • Serve as a senior Pfizer leader with the company's most strategically important payer customers, developing trusted relationships with senior customer executives and decision-makers.
  • Ensure Pfizer presents a coordinated and consistent enterprise approach to payer customers rather than fragmented product-by-product engagement.
  • Build a deep understanding of payer business models, economics, priorities, formulary strategies and evolving decision criteria.
  • Engage customers beyond transactional contracting discussions to understand emerging needs, identify areas of mutual value and strengthen long-term strategic relationships.
  • Represent Pfizer externally on complex access issues and ensure customer engagement reflects Pfizer's portfolio priorities and commitment to patients.
  • Personally engage in the highest-priority customer situations, negotiations and access opportunities where senior leadership is required.

3. Access Execution & Negotiation

  • Lead the translation of portfolio and brand access strategies into customer-specific negotiation and execution strategies.
  • Provide senior leadership and oversight for complex payer negotiations, ensuring account teams operate within established contracting frameworks, financial parameters and governance.
  • Lead or directly participate in the most strategically important customer negotiations and contracting discussions.
  • Partner closely with Access Enablement on offer development, deal analytics, scenario modeling, gross-to-net implications and contracting parameters.
  • Ensure customer negotiations reflect a clear understanding of the value of access, competitive dynamics and the economic implications of potential contracting decisions.
  • Make thoughtful tradeoffs across products, customers and portfolio priorities to achieve sustainable access and business outcomes.
  • Surface issues requiring escalation and provide senior leadership with clear choices, implications and recommendations.

4. Portfolio & Brand Access Execution

  • Partner with US Market Access BU leaders to understand portfolio and brand access ambitions and translate those priorities into customer-specific strategies.
  • Ensure payer teams understand the strategic intent behind brand access objectives and can effectively represent those priorities with customers.
  • Develop a portfolio view of access opportunities and challenges across payer accounts and identify where coordinated action can improve outcomes.
  • Enable differentiated account strategies across products and therapeutic areas based on market dynamics, competitive intensity and customer priorities.
  • Partner early on upcoming launches so account teams understand the evolving market, payer expectations, potential access barriers and customer-specific opportunities.
  • Support effective execution throughout the product lifecycle, adapting payer strategies as market, customer, competitive and policy dynamics evolve.

5. Customer & Market Intelligence

  • Establish Payer Account Management as a critical source of actionable customer intelligence for the broader US Market Access organization.
  • Maintain deep knowledge of the evolving U.S. payer environment, including payer and PBM business models, formulary strategies, benefit design, utilization management, consolidation and emerging access models.
  • Ensure account teams systematically capture, synthesize and communicate customer insights and emerging market signals.
  • Translate customer intelligence into clear implications for access strategy, contracting, launches, forecasting and portfolio planning.
  • Bring the payer perspective into business decisions while distinguishing between individual customer feedback and broader market trends.
  • Anticipate changes in customer strategies and proactively position Pfizer to respond to emerging access opportunities and risks.

6. Access Performance & Business Outcomes

  • Establish clear measures of payer account performance tied to access outcomes, account objectives and business priorities.
  • Monitor formulary positioning, access changes, contracting performance, account opportunities and emerging risks across payer customers.
  • Ensure account teams maintain a clear line of sight between customer activity, access outcomes and business impact.
  • Partner with Access Enablement, Finance, analytics and BU teams to assess the financial and gross-to-net implications of payer strategies and contracting decisions.
  • Provide senior leadership with regular visibility into customer performance, emerging risks, access changes and areas requiring intervention.
  • Drive accountability for execution and continuously adjust account priorities based on performance and market dynamics.

7. Launch & Lifecycle Readiness

  • Ensure payer account teams are prepared for upcoming launches with clear customer strategies, insight needs, engagement plans and execution priorities.
  • Bring early payer feedback into launch planning to inform access assumptions and identify potential barriers or opportunities.
  • Partner with BU access leaders and other market access capabilities to transition launch access strategy into disciplined customer execution.
  • Ensure payer engagement evolves appropriately across the lifecycle, from launch preparation and early access establishment through in-line growth and later lifecycle management.
  • Identify opportunities to use established payer relationships and portfolio knowledge to improve launch readiness and speed of execution.

8. Cross-Functional Leadership & Ways of Working

  • Establish strong ways of working across Payer Account Management, broader Strategic Account Management, US Market Access BU leaders and Access Enablement.
  • Clarify the handoffs between access strategy, contracting strategy/analytics and customer execution, creating clear accountability while maintaining integrated decision-making.
  • Serve as the senior payer execution partner to BU access leaders, ensuring that brand strategies can be effectively operationalized at the account level.
  • Partner with Medical, Health & Value, Patient Services, Market Access Operations, Finance, Legal, Compliance, Policy and other functions as appropriate to address complex customer and access issues.
  • Ensure customer-facing colleagues receive timely and consistent direction and that internal partners have visibility into meaningful customer developments.
  • Drive a One Pfizer approach to payer engagement, minimizing duplication and ensuring customers experience a coordinated enterprise relationship.

9. Organizational Leadership & Capability Building

  • Lead, inspire and develop a high-performing payer account organization capable of operating effectively in an increasingly complex customer environment.
  • Lead leaders and experienced account executives, setting clear expectations for performance, strategic thinking, collaboration and customer leadership.
  • Build capabilities in strategic account management, negotiation, financial acumen, payer economics, portfolio thinking and executive customer engagement.
  • Establish consistent account planning, customer engagement and performance-management disciplines across the organization.
  • Coach and develop colleagues and create meaningful opportunities for growth, succession and broader enterprise exposure.
  • Build a culture of accountability, curiosity, collaboration, inclusion and responsible risk-taking.
  • Ensure the organization continually evolves its capabilities, tools and ways of working to meet the changing needs of customers and the business.

Basic Qualifications

Candidate demonstrates a breadth of diverse leadership experiences and capabilities including: the ability to influence and collaborate with peers, develop and coach others, oversee and guide the work of other colleagues to achieve meaningful outcomes and create business impact.

  • Bachelor's degree required
  • 15+ years of experience required with Bachelors; 13+ years of experience required with MBA/MS/MPH/master's degree; 10+ years of experience required with PhD or JD
  • Extensive leadership experience within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, healthcare or managed-care industry, with significant experience in U.S. market access.
  • Demonstrated success leading payer account management, national accounts, managed markets or other senior customer-facing market access organizations.
  • Deep understanding of the U.S. healthcare environment, including commercial, Medicare and government payer dynamics.

We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.


About the Role:
CrowdStrike's marketing team is building an agentic AI platform that automates end-to-end workflows. Our mission is to reinvent how marketing works at CrowdStrike, giving teams the power to move faster, create smarter, and drive greater impact.

You will architect and build the infrastructure behind modern marketing execution, from AI agents and orchestration pipelines to unified data foundations, internal tooling, and production-grade integrations. You will turn high-friction workflows into durable operating systems that teams can trust and adopt at scale.

As a Sr. AI Growth Engineer on this team, you'll own the technical foundation of this platform. You'll build the integrations, infrastructure, UIs and tooling that delivers an enterprise-grade system used by marketing teams across CrowdStrike. You'll work directly with marketing leadership to ship production capabilities fast. This role is ideally suited for a builder who can pair product thinking with hands-on execution.

You will embed directly with marketing teams, building alongside the people doing the work to solve real operational pain points. Success in this role is measured not only by what you ship, but by workflows permanently transformed, adoption that sticks, and teams that become increasingly self-sufficient.

This role leads the Marketing Engineering pillar and reports directly to the VP of Marketing Excellence & Transformation. It offers rare greenfield ownership at the intersection of AI, marketing operations, and developer tooling, with direct visibility to senior marketing leadership.

Locations: Preference for candidates in Seattle, WA or located remotely on the West Coast.

What You’ll Do:

  • Build integrations: connecting the AI campaign engine to CrowdStrike's marketing stack — work management platforms (e.g., Workfront), marketing automation systems (e.g., Marketo), collaboration tools (Google Docs, Slack), CMS, and digital asset management systems

  • Develop the orchestration layer: that manages multi-agent pipelines, state persistence, error recovery, and parallel execution

  • Design and build intuitive web UIs: that make AI-powered workflows accessible to non-technical marketing users — campaign dashboards, workflow builders, approval interfaces, and real-time pipeline status views

  • Create production tooling: including HTML/email template generation from agent outputs, design asset pipelines (PPTX, PDF, SVG), and content publishing workflows

  • Build analytics infrastructure: performance dashboards, agent quality scoring, A/B test tracking, and feedback loops from distribution metrics back into the agent system

  • Design, build, and deploy custom AI agents: and agentic workflows that integrate AI APIs, MCP servers, automation platforms, and enterprise systems into our GTM motion

  • Implement auth, permissions, and multi-tenancy: so multiple marketing teams and campaign owners can run pipelines concurrently with appropriate access controls

  • Own CI/CD and reliability: automated testing for agent outputs, regression detection, deployment pipelines, monitoring and alerting

  • Optimize performance: caching, parallelization, and cost management for LLM API calls across high-volume campaign runs

  • Partner closely with Performance Marketing, Digital Intelligence, Engineering, and marketing leadership: to ensure the roadmap is technically sound, operationally meaningful, and connected to business outcomes

What You’ll Need:

  • 8+ years of full-stack engineering experience with Python and modern JavaScript or TypeScript

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field —or equivalent practical experience

  • Frontend engineering experience: you've built production web applications with React (or equivalent) and understand how to design interfaces that drive adoption with non-technical users

  • Production experience with LLM/AI APIs: you've built and shipped systems that call Claude, GPT, or similar models at scale, and you understand token management, rate limiting, error handling, reliability, and cost optimization

  • Demonstrated experience with AI agents: you've designed, built, and deployed agentic workflows that transformed real work, not just isolated experiments

  • Experience building evaluation frameworks: for AI systems, including prompt evals, output quality scoring, benchmarking, and testing against clear baselines

  • Strong systems design skills: you can architect a multi-service platform, design APIs, and make infrastructure decisions that hold up as the system scales

  • Integration experience: you've connected systems via REST APIs, webhooks, OAuth, and worked with enterprise tools (project management, CMS, marketing automation platforms)

  • A strong builder mindset: you would rather ship a working v1, learn quickly, and iterate than spend a quarter talking about what might be possible. You thrive in ambiguity, make smart architectural calls, and create clarity where none exists yet

  • Strong communication skills and a genuine ability to translate technical concepts for non-technical audiences

  • Working knowledge of CI/CD, containerization, cloud infrastructure, and observability (AWS preferred)

  • Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.

Bonus Points:

  • Experience with multi-agent AI systems, LLM orchestration frameworks (LangChain, CrewAI, Claude Code agents), or building AI-powered automation at scale

  • Experience working closely with marketing teams or building systems for marketers as end users — familiarity with work management platforms (e.g., Workfront, Asana), marketing automation systems (e.g., Marketo, HubSpot), CMS platforms, or the campaign lifecycle

  • Experience building internal platforms, developer tools, or self-service systems where other teams are your customers

  • Experience building workflow builders, drag-and-drop interfaces, or low-code/no-code platforms — an eye for UX and tools that non-engineers actually enjoy using

  • Familiarity with document and content pipelines — HTML email rendering, PDF or PPTX generation, structured publishing workflows, or turning structured data into polished visual outputs

  • Familiarity with vector databases, embeddings, retrieval systems, and RAG architectures

  • Background in marketing operations, RevOps, digital product management, personalization, or journey orchestration

  • Contributions to open-source AI or automation projects, or a track record of strong technical writing

  • Prior work in high-growth B2B SaaS or cybersecurity environments

jobs.excerpt: RemoteThe mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.
jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

An Ideal Candidate Should Have

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, including time leading a team or owning a major surface while staying hands-on
  • Rock solid Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android animations, Jetpack Navigation, and JUnit tests
  • Experience shipping and maintaining background audio or other long-running background work
  • Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing them, including what can't be covered by them
  • Something you introduced to a team that stuck after you stopped pushing it, and an honest account of what it cost to get there
  • Some comfort with the unpopular half of the job: asking people to change how they work, and living with the friction that follows
  • A view on which changes need heavy review and which don't, argued from what the system does
  • A track record of building things the rest of your team actually used, not only things that made you faster
  • The ability to describe how your team works with AI agents, not only how you do personally
  • Product design intuition, user empathy, and the drive to push Android UI/UX further than the spec asks for
  • Self-drive to improve the app and codebase beyond what's outlined in the spec
  • Excellent communication skills

Bonus

  • Building, maintaining, or contributing to open source Android projects
  • Experience with iOS, Web, or NodeJS

Technologies we use

  • Kotlin · Kotlin Coroutines · Kotlin Flow · Jetpack Navigation · Dagger 2 · Room · Custom Views, Canvas & Paint · Jetpack Compose · JUnit

Interview process

Several technical interviews plus an assessment on a real codebase. We aim to complete the process within 1 week.

Use the tools you use every day. A good part of the process is a walkthrough where you talk through your reasoning — why this approach, what you considered and dropped, where you were unsure.

Tell us more about yourself and why you're interested in the role when you apply.
And don’t forget to include links to your portfolio and LinkedIn.

Not looking but know someone who would make a great fit?

Refer them!

  • Stakeholder communication: You present status, risks, and trade-offs to leadership clearly. No surprises.

Technical & Architecture

You won’t write code daily, but you’ve built systems before and your engineers can’t bluff you. You can review a PR, challenge an RFC, and spot when a proposed architecture won’t scale.

  • Frontend Architecture: You understand modern frontend patterns: component architecture, state management, rendering performance, sdk's, observability, RUM, Feature flag and the challenges of building across multiple surfaces (web apps, browser extensions).

  • Service-Oriented Architecture: You understand how to decompose monoliths, define service boundaries, design API contracts, and manage inter-service communication patterns. You’ve lived through the trade-offs.

  • Domain-Driven Design: You think in bounded contexts, aggregates, and domain events. You can challenge your teams on whether their service boundaries reflect real business domains or just convenient code splits.

  • API Design: REST, event-driven, webhooks you’ve designed and reviewed APIs at scale. You have opinions on versioning, pagination, error handling, and contract testing.

  • Backend Systems: You’ve built or led teams building high-throughput backend services. You understand database design, caching strategies, message queues, and the operational realities of running services in production.

  • Infrastructure/Devops Awareness: You’re comfortable discussing containerization, CI/CD pipelines, cloud infrastructure (AWS), and deployment strategies. You don’t need to write Terraform, but you can review infrastructure decisions.

Quality & Engineering Excellence

You believe quality is a system, not a wish. You’ve built the processes and culture that make quality the default, not the exception.

  • Testing Culture: You’ve implemented testing standards (coverage targets, unit/integration/E2E requirements), enforced them through CI/CD gates, and shifted teams from “testing is QA’s job” to “testing is how we ship.”

  • Observability & Monitoring: You’ve driven observability practices: structured logging, metrics dashboards, alerting, and SLOs. You’ve used tools like DataDog, Grafana, or similar to make production health visible and actionable.

  • Definition of Done: You’ve built and enforced quality gates that teams actually follow not checkbox theater, but meaningful criteria that prevent regressions, improve code review quality, and ensure features are truly production-ready.

  • High-Performing Teams: You’ve built teams where engineering excellence is a cultural value, not a top-down mandate. Your teams write RFCs before building, review each other’s code rigorously, and take pride in operational reliability.

  • Continuous Improvement: You run retrospectives that produce real change. You track quality metrics (bug escape rate, incident frequency, deployment success rate) and use them to drive systematic improvement.

Nice-to-have

  • Hands-on experience with Go - you’ve built or shipped production systems in Golang

  • Hands-on experience with React and TypeScript you can review frontend architecture decisions with depth

  • Chrome Extension development experience or understanding of browser extension constraints

  • AWS production experience (Kubernetes, ECS, RDS, SQS/SNS, CloudWatch, Terraform)

  • Experience with Elasticsearch, Redis, or vector databases at scale

  • Background with SOC2 / ISO 27001 compliance from an engineering perspective

  • Experience managing remote-first, async-first engineering teams across EU/US timezones

  • B2B SaaS, API platforms, or sales intelligence product experience

You’ll Thrive Here If

  • You’ve transformed an engineering organization’s delivery culture AND raised its technical bar simultaneously

  • You build coalitions rather than issuing mandates - you understand that lasting process change requires buy-in, not authority

  • You obsess over team health metrics: sprint completion, cycle time, developer satisfaction, regrettable attrition

  • You see the Engineering Manager role as a craft, not a stepping stone you read about management, practice it deliberately, and measure your own improvement

Remote | Part-Time | 30 Hours/Week | $5-$6/hour

About the Practice

We are hiring a Virtual Medical Assistant to support a growing solo ophthalmology practice in the United States. The clinic needs a dependable, professional, and patient-focused team member who can help manage front desk communication, scheduling workflows, patient requests, and insurance-related support.

This is a patient-facing role. The selected candidate will serve as one of the first points of contact for patients and must be confident, courteous, organized, and highly reliable.

Primary Role Objective

The Virtual Medical Assistant will help reduce the clinic's front desk workload by ensuring that every patient call, voicemail, and request receives timely and accurate attention.

Success in this role means:

  • Patients receive professional and responsive assistance.

  • Calls and voicemails are answered or returned promptly.

  • Patient requests are documented and routed correctly.

  • Scheduling follows the clinic's triage protocols.

  • No important task or patient concern is dropped.

Core Responsibilities

Patient Calls and Voicemail Management

  • Answer inbound patient calls professionally and return missed calls or voicemails promptly.

  • Gather accurate patient information and determine the appropriate next action.

  • Escalate urgent or clinical concerns appropriately while maintaining a confident and courteous phone presence.

Patient Request and Task Management

  • Create to-do tasks in Practice Plus / Nextech for refill requests, patient concerns, and administrative follow-ups.

  • Route messages accurately to the physician, technician, or appropriate team member.

  • Monitor pending requests to ensure no patient concern is missed or left unresolved.

Triage-Based Scheduling

  • Assist new and established patients with appointment requests using the clinic's approved workflow.

  • Complete required triage steps before scheduling patients who require physician review.

  • Schedule or reschedule appointments accurately based on approved instructions and urgency guidance.

Patient Communication and Reminders

  • Send appointment reminder texts using approved clinic scripts through Reach UC.

  • Handle scheduling-related communication professionally and clearly.

  • Redirect clinical questions to the appropriate phone or clinical workflow without providing medical advice.

Team Communication and Reporting

  • Communicate clearly with the clinic team through Microsoft Teams regarding breaks, updates, and pending items.

  • Submit a daily end-of-day report summarizing completed tasks, unresolved concerns, and escalations.

  • Maintain consistent accountability, responsiveness, and schedule adherence throughout the shift.

Additional Responsibilities After Training

As the selected candidate becomes comfortable with the clinic's workflow, responsibilities may expand to include:

  • Verifying insurance eligibility and benefits through Medicare and commercial insurance portals.

  • Reviewing copays, deductibles, coinsurance, and expected patient responsibility.

  • Assisting the clinic in determining amounts to collect at the time of visit.

  • Supporting referral processing and patient scheduling from referral sources.

  • Following up on claim denials or billing concerns, as assigned.

  • Conducting professional balance collection calls for overdue patient accounts.

Required Qualifications

  • At least 1 year of U.S. healthcare administrative experience in a patient-facing role.

  • Experience handling patient phone calls, appointment scheduling, and voicemail follow-up.

  • Experience verifying insurance benefits, copays, deductibles, or patient responsibility.

  • Strong spoken and written English communication skills.

  • Professional, warm, and confident phone presence.

  • Strong attention to detail when documenting patient information and requests.

  • Ability to follow protocols carefully and escalate concerns appropriately.

  • Proven reliability, ownership, and follow-through.

  • Ability to work independently in a small clinic environment.

  • Availability to work the required Eastern Time schedule.

  • Reliable internet connection, functional computer, clear headset or microphone, and appropriate backup resources.

Strongly Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting an ophthalmology, optometry, retina, cataract, glaucoma, or eye care clinic.

  • Experience using Nextech / Practice Plus.

  • Experience using Reach UC or a similar medical phone and texting system.

  • Experience with triage-based scheduling workflows.

  • Familiarity with Medicare and commercial insurance portals such as Availity.

  • Experience supporting referrals, claim denials, or patient balance collections.

jobs.description:
Remote

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify's text-to-speech products to turn whatever they're reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify's text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview

Our Android app is the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, and the user base has grown faster than the way we build for it. We're looking for a Team Lead to own core product work and to raise how the team works around it.

This is a hands-on role, and we want to be clear about the split. You'll be writing code, reviewing code, and owning features of your own — that doesn't shrink when you take this job. The rest of it is the part that doesn't happen on its own: catching when three people have solved the same problem separately, deciding which version everyone should use, and making sure the team's time goes to the work that actually needs a decision. If you want to stop building, this isn't the role. If you want the code you write to be the smaller half of your impact, it is.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount.

What You'll Do

  • Own major features end to end, working closely with our design team — from the decision through to release. This is real delivery, not oversight
  • Own, maintain, and improve reliability metrics for key features
  • Review pull requests and give the kind of feedback people learn from, not just approval
  • Unblock the team: notice when someone has been stuck on the same thing for two days, and go take a look yourself
  • Notice when something one person built should become the version the team uses, and see that change through
  • Keep the shared pieces in working order — tested, clear enough for someone else to pick up, and consolidated when three versions of the same thing appear
  • Call it when the team is ready to change how it works, rather than waiting for that to happen on its own
  • Reduce how much manual intervention it takes to get a correct release out
  • When the same problem shows up twice, get the underlying setup changed so there isn't a third time
  • Shift verification left: grow what can be checked automatically so the nightly build going to QA is a confirmation rather than the first time anyone finds out
  • Run planning so the team's attention goes to the work that still needs decisions rather than the work that's already clear
  • Work out how much review each area needs, and where a person always signs off regardless
  • Participate in discussions across Product, Design, and Engineering, and bring the team's constraints into those rooms early
  • Handle critical issues, own feature releases, and provide nightly builds for the QA team
  • Make sure the people early in their careers are getting work they can learn from, and the time to learn from it

Some of your engineers will be skeptical about parts of how the team is asked to work. In our experience that skepticism tends to be specific and worth acting on, and the people raising it are often the right ones to hand the underlying problem to.

At Tether, we’re not just building products, we’re pioneering a global financial revolution. But that’s just the beginning:

Tether Evolution: At the intersection of technology and human potential, we are pushing the boundaries of what is possible, crafting a future where innovation and human capabilities merge in powerful, unprecedented ways.

Why Join Us?

Our team is a global talent powerhouse, working remotely from every corner of the world. If you’re passionate about making a mark in the fintech space, this is your opportunity to collaborate with some of the brightest minds, pushing boundaries and setting new standards. We’ve grown fast, stayed lean, and secured our place as a leader in the industry.

If you have excellent English communication skills and are ready to contribute to the most innovative platform on the planet, Tether is the place for you.

Are you ready to be part of the future?

About the job

Keet is a fully peer-to-peer messaging and video calling app built on Holepunch's P2P stack. There are no servers, no middlemen, and no data harvesting. People talk directly to each other, with end-to-end encryption by design.

We are looking for a Senior Technical Product Manager to own the vision for Keet and lead it to a billion users, competing head-on with WhatsApp and Telegram. This is not a maintenance role. You will define where Keet goes, convince the board and the team that it is the right direction, and then drive the execution that gets it there.

You are a rare combination of three things. You are a product visionary who has shipped consumer chat or calling apps at scale. You are a technologist who can go deep on P2P architecture and the Pear / Holepunch stack (docs.pears.com). And you are a hands-on builder who uses AI tools to prototype and prove concepts in days, not months. You set the bar high, move at incredible speed, and lead from the front.

You will also be the person who catches what others miss. The PM who thrives here reads every ticket, tracks every dependency, asks the uncomfortable question before it becomes a launch incident, and keeps five workstreams moving simultaneously without losing the thread on any of them.

If you prefer a PM role where you set strategy and delegate execution, this is not the right fit. If you want to build something that ships to real users, moves markets, and carries your fingerprints from concept to production, we want to hear from you.

Responsibilities

Vision & Strategy

  • Own and articulate the long-term product vision for Keet as the world's leading private, peer-to-peer communication app, with a clear path to 1 billion users.

  • Analyze WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, LINE, WeChat and emerging competitors to identify where P2P gives Keet an unfair advantage, and build the roadmap around it.

  • Present product vision, strategy, metrics and progress to the board and executive leadership with clarity and conviction.

Define a growth strategy across acquisition, activation, retention and virality, with measurable targets at every stage.

Technical Product Leadership

  • Develop a deep working understanding of the Holepunch P2P stack (Pear runtime, Bare, Hypercore, Hyperswarm, HyperDHT, Autobase, Hyperbee) and translate its capabilities and constraints into product decisions.

  • Partner with core engineering on hard P2P problems at scale, including NAT traversal, offline sync, multi-device support, large groups, push notifications, and battery and data efficiency on mobile.

  • Own the real-time calling experience (1:1 and group voice and video, plus screen sharing) to a quality bar that matches or beats Google Meet and Zoom.

  • Define clear feature tiers with explicit labels for stable versus experimental functionality.

Rapid Prototyping with AI

  • Use AI coding and design tools to build working prototypes and demos that prove concepts before committing engineering resources.

  • Turn ideas into something the team, users and the board can see and touch within days.

Execution & Team Leadership

  • Lead the product team and run the sprint cadence end to end, covering planning, prioritization, standups, reviews and retrospectives.

jobs.description:
The Role

We are seeking a LIHTC Year 15 Specialist to lead and manage investment dispositions, partnership restructurings, and investor exit strategies associated with Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) properties reaching the end of their initial compliance period. This role serves as a subject matter expert on Year 15 transactions and works closely with investors, developers, legal counsel, syndicators, asset managers, and ownership entities to evaluate and execute complex ownership transitions and preserve affordable housing assets.

The ideal candidate combines strong financial analysis capabilities with a solid understanding of LIHTC partnership structures, legal agreements, and transaction negotiations. This individual will be responsible for assessing investor exit options, modeling transaction outcomes, mitigating financial and tax liabilities, and facilitating successful resolutions among various stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage Year 15 and investor exit transactions across a portfolio of LIHTC investments.
  • Analyze partnership agreements, operating agreements, and related legal documents to determine ownership rights, purchase options, transfer provisions, and exit strategies.
  • Review and interpret complex lower-tier, middle-tier, and upper-tier partnership structures and ownership entities.
  • Build and maintain financial models to evaluate investor exit scenarios, partnership restructurings, asset dispositions, and portfolio strategies.
  • Perform valuation analyses, waterfall distributions, net present value (NPV) calculations, and sensitivity analyses to support transaction recommendations.
  • Review partnership tax returns, K-1s, capital accounts, and benefits schedules to assess financial impacts and potential investor tax liabilities.
  • Lead negotiations with developers, investors, syndicators, attorneys, and other stakeholders to facilitate Year 15 transactions and ownership transfers.
  • Evaluate purchase options, right of first refusal (ROFR) provisions, qualified contract considerations, and other exit mechanisms available under partnership agreements.
  • Partner with legal counsel to document and execute ownership restructurings, transfers, and investor exits.
  • Identify transaction risks and develop strategies to protect investor interests while supporting long-term affordable housing preservation.
  • Coordinate due diligence efforts, including financial, legal, and operational reviews.
  • Prepare investment committee memorandums, transaction summaries, and recommendations for senior leadership.
  • Maintain knowledge of LIHTC regulations, market trends, and industry best practices related to Year 15 transactions and affordable housing preservation.
  • Collaborate with Asset Management, Acquisitions, Legal, and Finance teams to optimize transaction execution and portfolio performance.

  • Experience working with institutional investors, syndicators, developers, and external legal counsel.
  • Knowledge of affordable housing preservation strategies and emerging Year 15 market trends.

Key Competencies

  • LIHTC Program Knowledge
  • Partnership Agreement Analysis
  • Legal Document Interpretation
  • Transaction Structuring
  • Negotiation & Influence
  • Critical Thinking
  • Risk Assessment

  • Project Management
